seo.title: Strategic Financial Advisory | DNH
seo.description: Examine the options and implications behind major financing, liquidity, capital structure, allocation and business-growth decisions.

sections.heading: Strategic Financial Advisory: make important decisions with greater clarity
paragraphs: Financing, investment and expansion decisions do more than change today’s numbers; they can reshape liquidity, risk and the future of the company.
Drawing on Dr Nasim Mohammadhassani’s specialist experience, DNH helps examine the options and financial implications behind important business decisions.

media.alt: A conceptual strategic financial advisory review

sections.heading: Strategic financial advisory goes beyond managing numbers and reports
paragraphs: Financial reports show the current position, but future decisions require an examination of the implications of each choice.
Strategic advisory helps owners and leaders understand options, constraints and risks before committing resources.

items.title: Define the financial issue
items.description: Clarify the central decision and the factors that affect it.

items.title: Examine the options
items.description: Compare financial paths against costs, obligations and risks.

items.title: Consider the future of the business
items.description: Assess effects on liquidity, capital structure and future plans.

sections.note: This service does not replace accounting, routine financial reporting or day-to-day finance management. Executive Briefings provide a separate, focused route for a defined leadership issue.

sections.heading: Which decision-makers can benefit from this service?
sections.intro: It is intended for people whose decisions can materially affect the resources, risk and future of a business or corporate group.

items.title: Owners and chief executives
items.description: You face an important expansion, financing or investment decision and want to examine its implications before acting.

items.title: Boards and finance leaders
items.description: You need a strategic review of financial options, risks and decision implications.

items.title: Holdings and corporate groups
items.description: Resources, debt and investments across different companies affect the group’s overall financial structure.

sections.heading: Which financial decisions call for strategic review?
sections.intro: A major financial decision can affect several parts of a business. Strategic review makes the links between resources, obligations and future plans clearer before action.

items.title: Financing and debt
items.description: Funding sources, financing costs and repayment obligations.

items.title: Liquidity and working capital
items.description: Cash resources, operating needs and capacity to meet obligations.

items.title: Business expansion
items.description: Capital needs and their impact on liquidity and financial capacity.

items.title: Capital allocation
items.description: Comparing investment priorities for limited financial resources.

items.title: Capital-structure review
items.description: The mix of debt and owner capital and the implications of change.

items.title: Owner and company capital
items.description: How company decisions affect owner capital, obligations and resources.

sections.heading: Profitability does not always mean sufficient liquidity
sections.intro: A business can report a profit while lacking the cash required for debt payments or operating costs.

groups.label: PROFIT AND CASH FLOW
groups.title: Recorded profit is not the same as cash received
bullets: Accounting profit records performance over a period
Cash flow shows when resources actually enter and leave
Credit sales may generate profit before cash is collected

groups.label: CAPITAL STRUCTURE
groups.title: Every source of finance creates future implications
bullets: The mix of owner capital and debt
Alignment between obligations and cash flow
Effects of expansion or borrowing on future flexibility

sections.heading: Which source of capital best fits the business circumstances?
sections.intro: Consider a company that needs new capital to expand. Each funding path has its own costs, obligations and implications.
sections.badge: DEMO | HYPOTHETICAL EXAMPLE, NOT COMPANY-SPECIFIC ADVICE

items.title: Borrowing
items.description: Can provide the required funds but creates financing cost and repayment obligations.
bullets: Can future cash flow support the repayments?

items.title: A partner or investor
items.description: Can reduce debt-service pressure but may affect ownership and decision rights.
bullets: What are the implications of changing ownership?

items.title: Internal resources
items.description: Can reduce external funding needs but may constrain operating liquidity.
bullets: How much can be used without placing operations under pressure?

sections.closing: No path—or combination of paths—is best without understanding the company’s financial position, constraints and objectives.

sections.heading: Which financial factors should be reviewed before a decision?
sections.intro: The capital amount is only one factor. Timing, financing cost, repayment capacity and risk all affect decision quality.

items.title: The genuine capital need
items.description: How much is required and where will it be used?

items.title: Timing of resources
items.description: When must capital be available and what timing constraints apply?

items.title: Cost and financial obligations
items.description: What costs, debt or commitments does each option create?

items.title: Liquidity and repayment capacity
items.description: How well do company cash flows align with future obligations?

items.title: Risk and economic scenarios
items.description: What happens if revenue, costs or economic conditions change?

sections.closing: The aim is to understand the interaction of these factors rather than choose a path on the basis of one number or upfront cost.

sections.heading: From defining the issue to comparing options and the path ahead
sections.intro: The engagement begins with the issue and business circumstances. Scope and service form are then defined around the need and decision complexity.

items.title: Initial assessment
items.description: Clarify the decision, urgency and fit with DNH’s services.

items.title: Define the engagement
items.description: Agree subjects, information, assumptions, output form and service boundaries.

items.title: Review the financial position
items.description: Understand liquidity, obligations, capital resources and relevant economic conditions.

items.title: Compare options and scenarios
items.description: Examine available paths and their possible implications.

items.title: Conclude and define the next step
items.description: Clarify priorities, material risks and matters requiring decision or further work.

sections.note: Implementation or decision follow-up is scoped separately. A review based on information supplied is not an audit or independent verification of the accounts.

sections.heading: What decision picture can the review provide?
sections.intro: Depending on the issue and agreed scope, the work can provide a clearer view of financial conditions, options, risks and action priorities.

sections.note: An illustrative decision note may show the issue, options, assumptions, limitations and next step. Output format, detail and delivery are agreed before specialist work begins.

sections.heading: Strategic advisory is not outsourced financial management
paragraphs: DNH focuses on important financial decisions, material risks and the options ahead.
Accounting and day-to-day finance management are outside this service. Implementation or periodic follow-up is considered only through a separate agreement.
The service does not guarantee financing, profitability or the success of a decision.

sections.heading: Facing an important financial decision? Understand the options first
paragraphs: If you face an important decision involving financing, capital structure, liquidity or business expansion, an initial assessment can be a useful starting point.
The decision and broad circumstances are clarified first so an appropriate specialist path can be defined where suitable.
sections.closing: You do not need to provide confidential documents or complete company financial information at the initial stage.
